# Alex Opak — Software Architect

> Personal blog of Alex Opak, software architect based in Zurich. 15+ years of experience in Ruby, Elixir, JavaScript, and distributed systems. Writes about AI architecture, expert systems, and the boundary between LLMs and deterministic decision-making.

## Posts

- [Expert in the Loop (EITL)](https://opakalex.github.io/posts/expert-in-the-loop/): Why Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) is a bottleneck, and how Expert-in-the-Loop with deterministic expert systems alongside LLMs offers a better paradigm for AI-driven decision making. Includes a Tln-language example for pull-request review automation.
- [LLM, Neural Network, or Expert System?](https://opakalex.github.io/posts/llm-neural-network-or-expert-system/): Each kind of system makes a different kind of decision. LLMs generate language, neural networks find patterns, expert systems make the call. Why the boundary matters, with a warehouse-replenishment example in the Tln language.
- [Enterprise AI Orchestration](https://opakalex.github.io/posts/enterprise-ai-orchestration/): Managing AI agents in the enterprise requires solving for security, knowledge access, and orchestration at once. Introduces OpenTalon -- an EITL-first framework that combines LLMs with expert rules -- and includes a Tln-language predictive-maintenance example for a warehouse forklift fleet.
- [Code Mode for MCP](https://opakalex.github.io/posts/code-mode-for-mcp/): LLMs are excellent at writing code, but bad at making business decisions. Cloudflare's Code Mode idea -- let the model write the script, and let an expert system run it -- is a natural fit for EITL. Includes a Tln-language claims-processing example for an insurance company.
- [Human-in-the-Loop, the Business-Comfort Zone, and Vigilance Theory](https://opakalex.github.io/posts/human-in-the-loop-vigilance/): HITL is sold as quality control but is really a business-comfort zone -- a moral crumple zone where a human absorbs the responsibility for decisions they cannot actually control. Walks through Sonar's 2026 verification-debt numbers, vigilance theory, and why pilots/AEC operators are experts not generic humans. Includes a Tln-language PR-review ruleset covering preview deploys, A/B checks, SQL EXPLAIN plans, ES p95 budgets, migrations, and metric-baseline gates.
- [Deterministic Where It Matters](https://opakalex.github.io/posts/deterministic-agent-pipeline/): Can a Tln + LLM agent pipeline promise same input, same output? LLMs are probabilistic by nature -- next-token sampling buys flexibility but never 100% accuracy. The answer is a split: decompose the pipeline into an LLM authoring edge (probabilistic, reproducible, verifiable) and a Tln decision core (provably deterministic, auditable, no model in the loop). Measure equality at the fact/decision level, not the token level. Covers opentalon-agents' authoring-vs-execution split, edge-triggered firing, grammar-constrained decoding, canonicalization, and includes a large Tln-language medical-triage pipeline with renal dosing, contraindication, allergy, and sepsis-escalation rules.

## Topics

- Expert-in-the-Loop (EITL) — a paradigm in which deterministic expert systems make decisions alongside LLMs, removing the human-review bottleneck for non-critical paths.
- Expert systems vs LLMs — the distinction between probabilistic language generation and deterministic, auditable rule-based decisions.
- [Tln language](https://tln-lang.org/) — a rule language used in the examples on this blog for declarative expert-system rules.
- [OpenTalon](https://github.com/opentalon/opentalon) — an EITL-first framework for enterprise AI agent orchestration: security-first request handling, channel-level auth (Teams/Slack/MCP), built-in RAG, and any-LLM compatibility.
- [opentalon-agents](https://github.com/opentalon/opentalon-agents) — persistent, LLM-authored automations written in Tln that run deterministically with no model in the loop: authoring-vs-execution split, edge-triggered firing, snapshot state between ticks, replay-safe restarts, poll/webhook/schedule triggers.
- Enterprise AI orchestration, RAG, predictive maintenance, AI security.
- Code Mode for MCP -- letting the LLM write a script (e.g. in Tln) instead of making the decision directly, then handing the script to an expert system that enforces rules and makes the call.
- Deterministic AI pipelines — same input, same output; decision determinism vs token-level determinism; probabilistic LLM authoring edge vs deterministic Tln decision core; reproducibility via greedy decoding, grammar-constrained generation, model pinning, prompt-hash caching, and canonicalization; auditability of automated decisions in medical, financial, and regulated domains.
- LLM hallucination, next-token prediction, temperature/sampling, verification and fact-checking of model output.
- AI architecture, software architecture, distributed systems.
